title: Inverse conjecture for the large sieve with additively structured sieving sets
statement:
Let $X$ be positive. For each prime $p<X^{1/2}$, let $\Omega_p\subseteq\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and let $A\subseteq[1,X]$ be obtained by sieving out the congruence classes in $\Omega_p$. Here a set $\Omega_p$ is **additively structured** if there is an $a\not\equiv0\pmod p$ such that

$$
\left|\sum_{x\in\Omega_p}e\left(\frac{ax}{p}\right)\right|\gg C_pp,
$$

where $C_p\gg\log^{-1}p$.

**Refined inverse conjecture for the large sieve.** Under these assumptions,

$$
|A|\ll X^\epsilon.
$$

The conjecture predicts that simultaneous additive structure in all the sieving sets forces the sifted set to be very small, refining the usual inverse large-sieve conjecture.
source_name: Farzad Aryan, “Distribution of squares modulo a composite number”, arXiv:1502.05062 (2015).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0807.5037](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.5037).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.05062

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).
